proposals.evidence: CDIAL 11515 vānara explicitly gives eastern bandara/bāndar and Nepali bā̃dar “monkey”, alongside regional transfer arrows. Survey bandor/bandara forms fit this family, with the borrowing route left open. The comparative family link retains uncertainty about transfer between Indo-Aryan languages.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 8376.1 *peṭṭa gives Hindi/Bengali peṭ and Oriya peṭa “belly”, distinct from poṭṭa and peḍḍuka. The survey pet spellings preserve the diagnostic e-vowel belly family, with the source’s dental-versus-retroflex transcription retained for audit rather than silently normalized in the data. The comparative family link retains uncertainty about transfer between Indo-Aryan languages.
